evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; direct scan inspection
evidence.field: 回 entry, printed p. 559; PDF p. 572; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0572/source.png
evidence.text: The entry identifies 回 as pictographic and says Shang–Zhou forms resemble a revolving loop; it describes Warring States Qin forms as two enclosed rings and says later forms follow them. It proposes rotation as the original meaning, then presents turning, changing direction, changing, returning, answering, taking a circuitous route, and counting occurrences as further uses. The cited examples include 荀子《致士》“水深而回,” 楚辭《離騷》, and 杜甫《百憂集行》. These are the book’s graphic and semantic analysis and cited literary examples; the passage does not establish dates for the examples or a securely dated earliest use. I inspected the headword, paragraph, form labels, cited references, and printed page number in the scan. The entry ends on this page; page 573 continues the neighboring 國 entry, not 回.

evidence.source: 香港中文大學漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 回: paleographic interpretation and cited literary examples
evidence.text: The entry interprets 商周 forms as revolving loops, reports two-ring Warring States forms, and proposes rotation as the original meaning. It quotes Shuowen’s “回，轉也” and cites examples from the Classic of Poetry, Xunzi, and Chu Ci. These are the database’s interpretation and textual examples, not a dated artifact sequence or a complete chronology of senses.

evidence.source: 臺灣學術期刊開放取用平台; 鄔可晶
evidence.text: The 2019 abstract proposes a competing analysis: 說文’s 古文 囘 and 篆文 回 were originally distinct graphs/words; 囘 represented “whirl,” while 回 was made for “around” and modeled on 圍. It further proposes that after clerical transformation 囘 was largely absorbed by 回, and says excavated Warring States and early Western Han texts use 回 for “around.” This is an attributed scholarly proposal from the abstract; the article PDF download required a captcha and was not inspected.
evidence.title: 說「回」 / A Discussion on the word “hui(回)”

evidence.source: 臺灣教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.field: A00727 回: Shuowen account, readings, and senses
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen explanation that 回 means turning and describes an outer 囗 with an inner form resembling rotation. It gives Mandarin huí and lists senses including turning, returning, answering, surrounding, and use as a counter for actions, periods, and chapters. Its gloss list and examples document the dictionary’s account; they do not alone establish when each sense arose.

gaps: No primary inscription image or securely dated contextual occurrence of 回 was inspected. 字源’s forms and period labels cite earlier paleographic compilations, but do not independently verify a dated artifact in this research.

The rotation/loop account is proposed by 字源 and CUHK; the exact depicted object remains unresolved. Wu Kejing’s distinct 囘/回 account is only available here as an abstract because the full text download was captcha-gated.
The 字源 entry gives a semantic extension account and cites literary examples, but the earliest attestation and chronology of the listed senses remain unresolved.
